title: South Warwickshire hotel named one of the most haunted in UK
excerpt: A historic South Warwickshire mansion has been named among Britain’s most haunted wedding venues
content:
Ettington Park named named one of the most haunted wedding venues in the UK

Published: 05:30, 31 October 2026

By Laura Kearns

A historic South Warwickshire mansion has been named among Britain’s most haunted wedding venues, with tales of ghostly figures, drowned children and unexplained sightings.

Ettington Park, a neo-Gothic mansion near Alderminster whose exterior featured as Hill House in the 1963 horror film The Haunting, is one of 10 venues highlighted by wedding planning platform Bridebook. The list comes as Google searches for “haunted wedding” have reportedly risen by 90 per cent over the past year, reaching more than 16,000 in the last month.

According to local legend, one of Ettington Park’s most famous spirits is Lady Emma, a former governess said to glide through the corridors in a white gown before disappearing into the walls.

Stories claim that she is searching for two children from the Shirley family, who owned the house and are said to have drowned in the nearby River Stour around 1800.

A servant girl named Mary is also rumoured to haunt the property. One guest reportedly saw a pair of feet beneath their bedroom door before opening it to find a distressed woman wearing a long grey dress.

The mansion’s cinematic connections add to its atmosphoeric reputation, making it an appealing setting for couples drawn to Gothic romance and a wedding venue with a darker history.

The other venues on Bridebook’s list include Hampton Court Palace, where the ghost of Catherine Howard, the fifth wife of Henry VIII, is said to scream through the corridors; and Lumley Castle in County Durham, where ghost stories have reportedly unnerved visiting international cricketers.

Other locations include Leeds Castle in Kent, Craig-y-Nos Castle in Wales, Warwick Castle, Walworth Castle in Darlington, Mosborough Hall in Sheffield, Farnham Castle in Surrey and the Bodleian Library in Oxford, where the ghost of Charles I is said to roam after being refused permission to borrow a book.

Zoe Burke, head of brand at Bridebook, said: “Every couple wants a venue with a story, and these ones have stories that have been told for centuries.”

She added that Gothic autumn weddings offered the chance to embrace candlelight, dark flowers and atmospheric settings, with the possibility of a few unexpected guests. Whether you believe a word of it or not, you’ll never have a more memorable first look than at the foot of a haunted staircase,” she said.
